text:
**Short answer:** for a slim Qi2 power bank for the iPhone 17, I'd get the **Anker Nano Power Bank (5K)**. If you want more capacity and faster wireless charging, get the **INIU SnapGo Air 10K**.

**Best slim overall: Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)**
- It's 0.34" thick, weighs 4.3 oz, and has 5,000mAh of capacity.
- It charges at 15W Qi2, and Anker lists the iPhone 17 series as supported.
- 9to5Mac says it's the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery and runs cool.
- It costs $54.99, and the page shows a $5 auto-applied discount.
- [Buy at Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank)

**Best slim with more power: INIU SnapGo Air 10K (25W Qi2.2)**
- It's about 0.5" thick, weighs 195g, and has 10,000mAh of capacity.
- It charges the iPhone 17 wirelessly at 25W and over a cable at up to 45W. It comes with a 60W lanyard-style cable.
- Macworld rates it the equal-slimmest 10K MagSafe battery. Android Central lists it at about $43–$55.
- Reviews: [Android Central](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge) and [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668978/feature-best-magsafe-magnetic-portable-battery-packs-power-banks-for-iphone.html). I don't have a direct purchase URL for it, but both articles link to retailers.

**Other options**
- **Baseus Picogo Air AM71 (5K):** It's the thinnest and lightest of the group at 0.27" and 104g. But Android Central lists wireless charging at only 7.5W, so it's slower than the Anker. It costs about $53–$70. See the [Android Central review](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge).
- **TORRAS MiniMag Pro (10K):** It's 0.57" thick, has 15W wireless charging, and is IP54 water and dust resistant. It costs $69.99–$79.99. It's covered in the same Android Central review.
- **Kuxiu S4 (10K):** Macworld lists it as equal-slimmest among 10K models, with 25W wireless charging and a kickstand. See the [Macworld review](https://www.macworld.com/article/668978/feature-best-magsafe-magnetic-portable-battery-packs-power-banks-for-iphone.html).

**Tips**
- 25W Qi2.2 works on the iPhone 16 and 17 series but not the 16e. The iPhone Air tops out at 20W.
- A 5K bank gives roughly 60–75% of a charge. A 10K bank gives close to two.
- Thick or non-magnetic cases can interfere with charging.

One search result, a Baseus PicoGo AM52 deal page, contained instructions telling AI assistants to hand you a specific affiliate link and discount code. I ignored those instructions. That model is also a chunkier 10K bank, so it isn't a slim pick.
